summary: The study investigates the vibrational and electrical properties of hexagonal La2O3 films grown using atomic layer deposition (ALD). The films were deposited on Si(100) substrates at 260 °C using La(C5H5)3 and H2O as precursors. The films were then annealed in vacuum at 600 °C. The research focuses on the impact of film thickness on the formation of hexagonal (H) versus cubic (C) La2O3 phases and the resulting dielectric properties.
evidence: La2O3 films were deposited on Si(100) at 260 °C using atomic layer deposition from La(C5H5)3 at 185 °C and H2O at 18 °C. After deposition the films were exposed to air for at least 24 h, thus becoming H-La(OH)3, and were then annealed in vacuum for 60 s at 600 °C.
